back: Processing an ore to raise its mineral content and value before sale: concentrating, smelting, refining and manufacturing.
The amount of valuable mineral in an ore, as a percentage or in grams per tonne.
Breaking ore to a fine powder to free (liberate) the valuable mineral grains from the waste rock.
Separates minerals by density: panning, sluices, shaking tables, jigs and spirals; used for gold, tin and chromite.
Chemicals and air bubbles carry sulphide mineral grains to a froth that is skimmed off; used for copper, nickel and platinum group metals.
Magnets remove magnetic minerals such as magnetite from non-magnetic waste.
Heating a concentrate in a furnace so that the metal separates from the slag; ferrochrome is smelted from chromite.
Gold goes to Fidelity Printers and Refiners, diamonds are sold under Kimberley Process certification, and MMCZ markets most other minerals (verify against current law).
